mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 318is engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 318is engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£3,200 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, or £2,500-£4,500 fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from around £550-£1,400, while reconditioned units range from £1,200 to £2,000 depending on the engine code.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 318is?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning is a rattling noise from the front of the engine, particularly between 3,000-4,000 RPM. As wear progresses, the rattle becomes more persistent and may be accompanied by a check engine light or, in severe cases, engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 318is?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and the car's condition. For an E36 318is valued at £3,000-£6,000, a full rebuilt engine at £1,800-£3,200 may represent 50-100% of the car's value - often making a used engine or repair the better option. For an E30 318is in good condition (valued £4,000-£15,000), replacement is more easily justified.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M42 and M44 engines in the 318is?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M42 (1989-1995) is a 1.8-litre 16-valve DOHC engine producing 136-140hp. The M44 (1996-1999) is its evolution - a 1.9-litre 16-valve DOHC engine also producing 140hp but with a DISA variable intake system and a new generation of engine management.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 318is engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 3 Series 318is engine replacement takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop, assuming the replacement engine is already in stock. The E30 and E36 generations require approximately 8-12 hours of labour.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 318is replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt and reconditioned BMW 3 Series 318is engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a shorter warranty (30-90 days) depending on the supplier - always confirm exact terms before purchasing.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 318is - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 318is was introduced as the sporty four-cylinder variant of the 3 Series, positioned between the standard 318i and the six-cylinder 325i. The "s" denoted a four-valve-per-cylinder engine with twin overhead camshafts - a significant step up from the eight-valve M40 and M43 engines fitted to the standard 318i. The 318is was produced across two generations: the E30 (1989-1991) and the E36 (1991-1999), with a mid-life engine update from the M42B18 to the M44B19 in 1996.
historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 318is is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: 1.8-litre Petrol (1989-1995, E30 & E36 pre-facelift)
items.commonFailure: The M42's timing chain tensioner and guide rails are a well-documented weak point. The intermediate plate that holds the timing chain idler gear can crack and fail. As an interference engine, timing chain failure causes valves to hit pistons, often writing off the cylinder head. The original M42 tensioner design is prone to rattle; upgrading to the later M44-style tensioner is a common preventative fix.

items.title: 1.9-litre Petrol (1996-1999, E36 facelift)
items.commonFailure: The M44 is an evolution of the M42, sharing many of its timing chain vulnerabilities. The DISA (Differentiated Intake System) valve fitted to the M44 can fail, causing a rattle and potential loss of low-end torque. Cooling system issues - particularly the plastic heater flange on the back of the cylinder head - are a known failure point on the M44, with failure leading to rapid coolant loss and overheating.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 318is Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 318is was fitted with two generations of BMW's four-cylinder 16-valve engine - the M42B18 (1989-1995) and the M44B19 (1996-1999). Both are interference engines, meaning timing chain failure is catastrophic. The M42 and M44 are now classic engines, and parts availability - while still good - is not what it was when these cars were new. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing components and are backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Guide Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 318is M42 and M44 Wear Prematurely
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 80k-120k (though many fail earlier or later depending on maintenance)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner on both the M42 and M44 is prone to failure, allowing the chain to slacken. The intermediate plate that holds the timing chain idler gear can crack and fail. As an interference engine, chain failure causes valves to hit pistons - often writing off the cylinder head. Upgrading to the later M44-style tensioner is a common preventative fix for the M42.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best caught early - before chain failure causes valve damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain has failed or engine is high-mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series 318is E30 is worth approximately £4,000-£15,000 depending on condition. An E36 318is is worth roughly £3,000-£8,000. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: used engine or timing chain repair typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your 318is has timing chain rattle but the engine hasn't suffered valve damage, a specialist timing chain replacement with the upgraded M44-style tensioner (£800-£1,400) is often the most cost-effective solution. If the chain has already failed and the cylinder head is damaged, a used or reconditioned engine is usually the sensible path. For E30 examples with rising classic values, a rebuilt unit is a justifiable investment.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failures - Plastic Components & Overheating on the 318is
problems.rootCause: The M42 and M44 cooling systems use plastic components that become brittle with age. On the M44, the plastic heater flange on the back of the cylinder head is a notorious failure point - it can crack and cause rapid coolant loss, leading to overheating. Water pump failure and expansion tank cracks are also common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, hoses, heater flange
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative maintenance - recommended every 60k miles or 10 years

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new cooling system components, warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating has caused head gasket failure or warped head

problems.recommendation: On any 318is, particularly the M44, a cooling system overhaul is one of the best preventative investments you can make. The plastic heater flange on the M44 is a ticking time bomb - replace it proactively along with the water pump and thermostat. If the car has already overheated, assess the cylinder head for warpage before deciding between a head gasket repair and a full engine replacement.
